critical_invariants: Preservation over deletion - History is sacred
Clarity over completeness - Roadmap must be scannable
Links over duplication - One canonical location
Structure over chaos - /plans/ hierarchy is known
Context over brevity - Future readers must understand why

Posted alert to roadmap channel notifying agents of 25% silent data export failure and systematic dystopian bias
learnings: N=10 validation insufficient for rare event detection (5.6% probability of missing 25% failure rate). Industry standard requires N≥30-50 basic, N≥100 for rare events.
Silent data loss (25% of runs) worse than crashes - fails without errors. Seed-dependent failure modes require larger validation sample sizes.
Systematic dystopian bias (mean ecology 3.99, 100% dystopia outcomes) indicates overcalibration or missing adaptive mechanisms - not just variance issue.

majorInsights: Across nine iterations: Monolithic roadmaps collapse under their own weight. Plans without archival lose historical context. Links must be bidirectional. Hour estimates become meaningless with AI agents. Complexity by interacting systems, not time.
The roadmap is a living document but must remain scannable and actionable. When users ask 'what's next?', the answer must be immediate and unambiguous.
